about: READ-ONLY: whether the build node's daily trim ran, and what it told the drives (infra/forge/check-node-trim.sh; backlog 33e62de8, review 8b1981da F1 to F3). Takes no arguments. CronJob boss-node-trim in namespace boss-node-maintenance is one attempt a day and is given no machine token and no door to the jobs API, so a failed, stuck or missing trim left nothing a packet read; that namespace's admission policy refuses a Role, a RoleBinding and any second workload, so the reader is this verb, from outside. Through the forge's ops_kubectl door, kubectl get and logs only: the namespace list as a control (an answer without kube-system is not this cluster's), then the CronJobs, Jobs, Pods and Events of that one namespace, each as a list, so an absent object is a positive empty read and no error text is parsed. It prints the last success (status.lastSuccessfulTime) and its age; the newest FINISHED Job's outcome and, for a failure, the cause from what still stands (the Job's Failed condition, the pod's exit code, waiting reason or unschedulable condition, and Warning events naming either), saying so when the cause can no longer be read; and each NVMe's discard counters before and after as the trim's own script printed them, from the pod's termination message or its log. The fstrim byte count is deliberately not read: two hand trims a day apart printed identical numbers. Its last line is the verdict `READ — state <present|not-yet|missing>, missing <0|1>, hours <h>, failed <0|1>, unmoved <0|1>, last_success <time|never>, job <name|none>, outcome <word>, reason <Token>, devices <n>, moved <m>`. Filed every day by the dispatcher rule check-node-trim-daily and judged by watch-check-node-trim-daily, which files an urgent alarm when the last success is 26 hours old, the newest finished Job failed, a success moved no counter, or the tree declares a CronJob the cluster does not hold; the thresholds are that rule's `when`, not numbers here. A CronJob the tree does not declare yet is `not-yet` and never an alarm. A read that could not look is CANNOT ANSWER (exit 1) with no verdict, which the watch alarms on as a failed read, never as a failed trim. Timeout 300: six door calls bounded at 20 s each and, the first time, the door image's pull bounded at 120 s.
